questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing The Living World. the basic unit of classification is:
questions.explanation: Species is the basic taxonomic category.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Biological Classification. the cell wall of fungi is mainly composed of:
questions.explanation: Fungal cell walls characteristically contain chitin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Plant Kingdom. the dominant phase in bryophytes is the:
questions.explanation: Bryophytes have a dominant, independent gametophyte.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Animal Kingdom. animals with a notochord at some stage belong to:
questions.explanation: The notochord is a defining chordate feature.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Morphology of Flowering Plants. the arrangement of ovules within the ovary is called:
questions.explanation: Placentation describes ovule arrangement in the ovary.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Anatomy of Flowering Plants. water and mineral transport in angiosperms occurs mainly through:
questions.explanation: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Structural Organisation in Animals. the epithelium lining alveoli is primarily:
questions.explanation: Thin simple squamous epithelium facilitates gas diffusion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Cell: The Unit of Life. the plasma membrane is best described by the:
questions.explanation: The membrane has a fluid lipid bilayer with embedded proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Biomolecules. the monomers of proteins are:
questions.explanation: Proteins are polymers of amino acids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Cell Cycle and Cell Division. crossing over normally occurs during which stage of meiosis I?
questions.explanation: Crossing over occurs in pachytene of prophase I.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Photosynthesis in Higher Plants. the oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from:
questions.explanation: Photolysis of water releases oxygen during the light reactions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Plant Growth and Development. the plant hormone commonly associated with cell elongation is:
questions.explanation: Auxins promote cell elongation in many plant tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Digestion and Absorption. the enzyme pepsin acts mainly in the:
questions.explanation: Pepsin is a gastric protease active in acidic conditions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: December challenge: During winter revision and annual assessment planning, a Class 11 learner is reviewing Breathing and Exchange of Gases. most oxygen in human blood is transported:
questions.explanation: Most oxygen binds reversibly to haemoglobin in red blood cells.
